_note: How a figure holds a gun (src/game/hold.ts, src/game/mannequin.ts). The animation library is a pistol library: it has no rifle clips, so a long gun is not held by the clips at all. It is hung off the chest and both arms are reached onto it, which means every number about where it hangs is one of ours and belongs here rather than buried in the code. The old ones put the grip five centimetres INWARD of the shoulder, and since a rifle's stock is behind its grip, the stock ended up beside the neck and through the chest, which is what the owner saw. A stock belongs in the shoulder pocket, which is outboard of the neck, and a gun long enough to reach past that has to sit further forward.

hold._out: how far outboard of the shoulder joint the grip sits, metres: the shoulder pocket, not the collarbone
hold._drop: how far below the shoulder joint the grip sits, metres
hold._forward: how far in front of the shoulder the grip sits at rest, metres, before any gun that needs more
hold._stockAllow: how far behind the shoulder joint a stock may sit, metres. A stock IS in the shoulder, and the gun hangs outboard of the joint where the torso is not, so the butt passes BESIDE the chest rather than through it: this is what lets it be 18 cm and not zero. Past it the gun is pushed forward until it clears, which is why a sniper stands with its hands further out than an SMG.
hold._maxForward: and how far forward that pushing may ever go, metres: past this the support hand cannot reach the handguard, and a hand that cannot reach its hold is the floating hand

lower._note: the long gun lowered and canted across the body for a sprint or a swap

reach._note: how fast a hand takes its hold and lets go, per second: the grip is quicker than the support hand, because a gun coming up is gripped before it is steadied

_throwShown: How long, s, a figure shows a grenade throw after it leaves the hand (src/main.ts localAct): the overhand throw clip is 1.1 s and plays at 1.3x, so this is its arm coming over and through, and a throw reads on other players' screens as a throw rather than a gun lowered for a moment.
_athleticJump: Horizontal speed, m/s, above which a figure in the air plays the athletic jump (the free library's NinjaJump_Idle_Loop, legs tucked) instead of the plain one. Sprint is 6.6 m/s (260 hu/s), so this is faster than a sprint: a slide jump, a pad, a hop chain, not a jump from a standing start or a walk.
_doubleJump: A double jump seen on a figure: its knees come up and go back down as it jumps again, over `time` seconds, the thighs raised `raise` degrees and the knees bent `bend` more at the top, eased (up then down), the body upright. The owner, 2026-09-30, first "there should be an animation for when we double jump for sure", then, of the front flip it first was: "I don't like the flip for double jump. People will double jump all the time and that's hard to hit I assume. Can we just have the legs raise a bit at the same time as the double jump, so there's something there?" SpeedKills' double jump rises for 0.39 s (movement.speedkills.json: sqrt(2 x 52 / 690)), so the knees are down again before its top. A figure first seen with a count of them does not lift for it. Ours.
_flatFeet: Standing or crouched still, the soldier's clips hold its toes 16.1 degrees up from its bind pose, so it stood on its heels (measured by apex-lobby for the battle royale's card, Milestone 416: the foot-to-ball line 30.5 degrees down against 46.6 bound, the ankle 0.152 m up and the ball 0.072; the owner asked it fixed). Under `under` m/s each foot is turned back until its toe is no higher than the bind pose has it, eased in and out at `rate` a second (rifle-hold soldiers only; the legacy figures keep their clips). A foot the clips point down (a crouch's kneeling foot) and every moving foot are the clips' own: walking and running, the planted feet come down flat by themselves (measured: 2 to 8 degrees at mid stance). Turned flat, a standing sole was 11 to 22 mm into the floor (its heel had been 44 mm in, the toe 9 above): the standing clip holds the legs lower than a walk's planted foot (the ankle 0.152 m up against 0.174), so a figure standing still is also lifted `lift` m, eased the same way (measured off the boots' lowest skin; not crouched, whose kneeling foot is already above the floor).
_headUp: The soldier's head held up to where it looks (the owner, 2026-10-04: from behind "their head is all tucked down, like chin is to the player's chest, making a headshot from the boog in the back almost impossible"). The clips carry the head down with the chest: measured, the head's middle 43 degrees forward of the neck standing, 52 to 56 aimed, 74 to 80 crouched or sprinting, and from 30 m behind at a standing eye a shot at the back of the head it showed was a headshot 66 times in 100 standing, 40 to 60 aimed and 2 to 7 crouched or sprinting (the neck's and the torso's volumes took the rest). Each frame the Head bone is turned about the figure's left so the face looks at the look's pitch, level when not aiming, `hold` of the way, never more than `most` degrees; before the deliberate tilts on top (a flinch, the aimed nod, the rifle rig's cheek on the stock). Not in an emote, a finisher, down or dead.
